verdict: The note establishes a fact that should alarm every downstream consumer of this model's policy quantities — the warm start, not the equations, selects which converged economy is delivered — but it argues the case entirely in engineer's units (training loss, HJB residuals, year-60 investment LEVELS) and never confronts the two economies with economics. As written, a climate economist cannot tell whether the nber economy is a feasible alternative optimum or an infeasible artifact of the documented value-level non-identification: no consumption, emissions, temperature, transition-timing, R&D-share, or SCC-like quantities appear anywhere; the headline "2x green / 4x dirty investment" is stated in year-60 levels that conflate policy rates with 60 years of compounded AK growth; and the +0.6 welfare gap is, in this model's units (V is permanent log-consumption), an ~82% permanent-consumption equivalent between two solutions of the SAME planner problem — prima facie implausible and demanding a simulated-welfare audit. The decisive arbitration the note says is impossible ("accuracy does not arbitrate") is in fact available: the planner's problem is a maximization, so a Monte-Carlo rollout of each frozen policy under the same model, compared to each network's own claimed V(x0), settles which economy is real without trusting residuals. Major revision: add the economic-moments comparison in rates and ratios, the resource-constraint feasibility audit, the cross-policy welfare rollout, and the inherited-calibration test for the nber arm.
major_points: Units and compounding: the headline '2x green, 4x dirty' compares year-60 investment LEVELS (I_g=133 vs 68; I_d=19 vs 4.8, units unstated). Under AK dynamics a modestly higher investment RATE compounds into a large level gap by year 60 (a ~1.2%/yr growth differential alone doubles levels). The economically meaningful objects are the rates i^g, i^d, i^r (per unit capital) and the ratios I_j/Y and C/Y; the note reports none of them. This is the same level-vs-ratio conflation that has produced false alarms in this project before.

No resource-constraint accounting: 2x green + ~4x dirty + ~2x R&D investment must all come out of the same AK output, C/K = (A_d - i^d)(1-Z) + (A_g - i^g)Z - i^r with A_d = 0.1303. Whether the nber economy is even feasible (C/K > 0 everywhere) and plausible (consumption share of output not collapsing) is unverified. Without min-along-path C/K and the C/Y path, 'a coherent alternative' is asserted, not shown.

The welfare gap is economically enormous and untreated: with flow utility delta[log C - log N], V is in permanent-log-consumption units, so Delta V = +0.6 in every jump state is an exp(0.6)-1 ~ 82% permanent-consumption-equivalent gap between two claimed solutions of the same maximization problem. Either one solution is wrong or the level is riding the documented delta-anchor null direction (residual cost of a common shift is only delta*0.6 = 6e-3). The note must decompose the value gap into a common constant plus shape, and confront both levels with simulated discounted utility.

The decisive arbitration exists and was not run: because the planner's problem is a max, freeze each policy, roll it out by Monte Carlo under the same model and penalty, and compare (a) realized welfare across policies and (b) each network's V(x0) against its own policy's realized value. HJB residuals cannot select between fixed points; realized welfare can. The note's conclusion that 'accuracy does not arbitrate' concedes defeat one experiment too early.

No climate side of the ledger: 4x dirty investment means a larger K^d path, hence higher emissions E = eta*A_d*(1-Z)*K, faster temperature rise, and earlier entry into the damage-jump window [1.5, 2.5] deg C. An economy with 4x dirty capital accumulation AND higher welfare in every state needs an explicit reconciliation (does its doubled R&D buy an earlier tech jump that outruns the damage risk, since J_tech = R in arrival units?). Temperature, emissions, and expected jump-time paths must be reported for both economies.

The quantities policy consumers actually need are absent: an SCC-like object (-V_y normalized by marginal utility delta/(C/K), in consumption units), the green-transition timing (first passage of Z past e.g. 0.9), and the R&D share of output. If these differ by ~2x across warm starts, that -- not the training-loss table -- is the finding that matters to the integrated-assessment audience, and it should be the abstract.

Inherited-calibration confound: the winning warm start is a trained solution of a DIFFERENT (4-state NBER legacy) calibration. The 'alternative solution' may simply be that economy's investment behavior persisting through fine-tuning. The note must compare the nber-arm's delivered paths to the legacy model's own solution: if the nber arm is closer to its parent than to the reference, the result is inherited bias wearing a low residual, which changes the interpretation from 'multiple solutions of this model' to 'training cannot escape the pretraining economics'.

The nber solution's 10x-lower pre-damage pre-tech HJB error is evaluated along the REFERENCE's simulated path -- states the reference policy visits, not states the nber policy visits. Symmetric evaluation (each solution's error along its OWN path, and each along the other's) is required before the 'even favors the alternative' claim; a smooth wrong solution can look good off its own support.
minor_points: State units and normalization of I_g, I_d (levels in the K_0 = 880 normalization? per year?) in every table and figure caption.
This is the pi = 1 one-jump variant, not the paper's pi = 0.04 baseline; say so prominently and caveat external validity of the selection finding to the 6-regime baseline.

The marginal-value ratios (V_logK x1.6, V_logR x1.8) 'rationalize' the higher investment only if C/K moves consistently through the FOC delta/(C/K) = phi'(i)[V_logK - Z V_Z]; show the FOC arithmetic at 3 path points instead of asserting it narratively.

Report the uncertainty-neutral (xi = infinity) comparison alongside xi = 0.05: the level non-identification is amplified by 1/xi in the jump distortion, so if the nber-reference gap shrinks at xi = infinity that localizes the mechanism.

The jump-exponent clamp to [-60, 60] was added to all RCT arms but the reference was trained without it; one sentence on why this does not break comparability (clamp claimed inactive on non-overflowing arms -- show the activation count is zero for nber/perturb).

The analytic-arm post-mortem is good; state explicitly that the fix (jump-consistent shape) exists and was not tested, rather than leaving 'a shape-aware variant would be the fix' in the study log only.

Within-method seed spread of 12% for perturb is dismissed as 'the one exception' -- but it is the same order as many economic differences of interest; report seed spread in the same economic units demanded above.

demanded_experiments.name: Cross-policy Monte-Carlo welfare rollout (the arbiter)
demanded_experiments.design: Freeze the policy networks of the reference and of nber_s1 (and nber_s2 as a replication). For each policy, simulate N = 10,000 paths from the paper initial condition (K0=880, Z0=0.7, Y0=1.1, R0=11.2) at xi = 0.05 for 400 years (until e^{-delta t} truncation error < 1e-3 of V), simulating the Brownian shocks, the tech jump (intensity R, pi = 1), and the damage jump (intensity J_n(y)), with the robust objective evaluated consistently: either (i) under the distorted measure implied by each policy's own h and g with the xi-penalty flow terms added, or (ii) as the simpler uncertainty-neutral check at xi = infinity for both. Compute realized J_hat = E[integral e^{-delta t} delta(log C_t - log N(Y_t)) dt + penalties] with MC standard errors. Hold the model, parameters, and shock draws (common random numbers) fixed across policies.
demanded_experiments.decides: Two statistics: (a) |V_net(x0) - J_hat(own policy)| for each solution -- the solution whose claimed value matches its own rollout within 2 MC standard errors is internally consistent, the other is not; (b) J_hat(nber policy) vs J_hat(reference policy) under common random numbers -- since the planner maximizes, the higher realized welfare identifies the better policy. This settles which economy is real; it is also the single figure that settles the note (four bars: claimed V and realized J per solution, with MC bands).

demanded_experiments.name: Economic-moments table in rates and ratios
demanded_experiments.design: For both converged economies (reference, nber_s1) at xi = 0.05 and xi = infinity, along the mean simulated path, report at t = 0, 30, 60: i^g, i^d, i^r (rates per unit capital), I_g/Y, I_d/Y, I_r/Y and C/Y (Y = A_d K^d + A_g K^g output), Z_t, emissions E_t, temperature Y_t, and cumulative damage-jump probability 1 - exp(-integral J_n dt). Add first-passage times: median year Z crosses 0.9 and median tech-jump arrival year. Everything else (paths, seeds) as already simulated.
demanded_experiments.decides: Whether the two economies differ in POLICY RATES or only in compounded levels: if i^g differs by, say, <20% while the year-60 level differs 2x, the headline must be rewritten as a growth-rate difference. Also whether C/Y stays in a plausible band (roughly 0.55-0.85 for this calibration) for both.

demanded_experiments.name: Resource-constraint feasibility audit of the nber economy
demanded_experiments.design: Along every simulated nber path (all 10k paths, all t), evaluate C/K = (A_d - i^d)(1-Z) + (A_g - i^g)Z - i^r pointwise from the delivered control networks (regime-correct A_g and the -i^r term only in R&D-active regimes). Report min over paths x time, the 1st percentile, and the full C/K time profile vs the reference's.
demanded_experiments.decides: min C/K > 0 with margin (no path within, say, 20% of zero consumption) is necessary for the nber economy to be a feasible economy at all; a violated or knife-edge constraint reclassifies it as an artifact regardless of its residual.

demanded_experiments.name: SCC-like marginal-damage object across solutions
demanded_experiments.design: Along each economy's own mean path and at the common initial state, compute the marginal willingness to pay to reduce emissions: MWTP_t = -V_y(x_t) / (delta/(C_t/K_t)) x (units conversion to per-ton), using each solution's own V_y (with the regime-correct (logN)_y transform per PAPER_HJB_REFERENCE). Report the ratio nber/reference at t = 0, 30, 60 and across xi in {infinity, 0.1, 0.05}.
demanded_experiments.decides: The statistic policy consumers care about: if the SCC-like object differs by ~1.5-2x across warm starts, warm-start selection contaminates the model's central policy output and must be the headline; if it agrees while investments differ, the disagreement is confined to the (weakly identified) intertemporal margin.

demanded_experiments.name: Analytic-corner benchmark for the marginal value of capital
demanded_experiments.design: On the slice Z = 0.98, Y = 0 (climate externality negligible), xi = infinity, evaluate V_logK for both solutions and compare to the exact full-green BGP benchmark v_logK = 1 (log-utility AK closed form; also compare implied i^g against the closed-form BGP investment rate). Hold everything else at delivered checkpoints; no retraining.
demanded_experiments.decides: Which value function respects a known exact benchmark: |V_logK - 1| at the corner, per solution. Since the two solutions differ by x1.6 in V_logK, at most one can be near the analytic bound; this is a cheap, assumption-free tiebreaker on shape (complementary to the level audit in the rollout).

demanded_experiments.name: Inherited-calibration (parent-proximity) test for the nber arm
demanded_experiments.design: Simulate the legacy 4-state NBER-calibration model's own delivered solution (the warm-start parent, pretrained/nber_legacy) under ITS calibration, and separately evaluate the nber-arm policies at the current calibration's states. Compute normalized path distances d(nber_arm, parent) and d(nber_arm, reference) over the moment set of experiment 2 (rates and ratios, not levels). Same simulation harness, common initial condition mapped appropriately.
demanded_experiments.decides: If d(nber_arm, parent) << d(nber_arm, reference), the 'alternative converged economy' is the parent calibration's economics surviving 1M iterations of fine-tuning -- inherited bias, not evidence of multiplicity in THIS model -- and the note's Finding 2 must be reframed accordingly.

initialization_proposals.name: Jump-consistent continuation-value initialization (fixed anchor)
initialization_proposals.construction: Train regimes backward as now. For each pre-jump regime, initialize the value network by regression onto the probability-weighted continuation value of its OWN already-trained immediate successors (pre-damage pre-tech onto pi*V'' + (1-pi)*V' and the damage-jump mixture; NOT the terminal post-post value for every regime, which is what the failed 'anchor' arm did). This makes V' - V ~ 0 at initialization, so g = exp(-(V'-V)/xi) ~ 1 and the 1/xi amplification that destroyed the analytic arm is absent by construction. Controls initialized by solving the three FOCs pointwise given the initialized value's gradients (Newton on the closed forms in section 8).
initialization_proposals.rationale: Directly repairs the diagnosed failure mechanism of both failed arms (analytic: right level, wrong shape, overflowed through the jump exponent; anchor: wrong target -- terminal value is the wrong shape for R&D-active regimes since it lacks logR structure). Uses no external trained solution, so it cannot import another calibration's economics; if it converges and lands on one of the two existing basins, that is evidence about which basin is the natural one.

initialization_proposals.name: Coarse finite-difference warm start (independent-method anchor)
initialization_proposals.construction: Solve each regime on a coarse tensor grid by finite differences at fixed xi = 0.05, lambda_3 fixed per slice: the 3-state post-tech regimes with the existing FD+ADI code, the 4-state R&D-active regimes on a coarse grid (e.g. 41x41x31x31, false-transient sweep) -- accuracy target only ~1e-2, it is an initializer not a solution. Regress value and control networks onto the FD solution (5-10k supervised steps), then run the standard 1M schedule.
initialization_proposals.rationale: The only proposal that pins level AND shape from a method with no neural lineage and no other calibration. If FD-started training lands on the reference, the reference is vindicated; if it lands on nber, the reference is the artifact; if on a third point, multiplicity is worse than reported. Given the study's own conclusion that a warm start is REQUIRED, an independent-solver warm start is the scientifically clean one.

initialization_proposals.name: xi-homotopy curriculum (the M6 arm that was designed but never run)
initialization_proposals.construction: Stage 0: train from cold at xi = infinity only (drop the -1/(2xi) drag and set g = 1; the uncertainty-neutral HJB, a much better-conditioned problem). Stage k: restart from stage k-1 weights with the logxi sampling window slid down one decade (infinity -> 1 -> 0.1 -> 0.05), 250k iterations per stage, everything else at the reference config. Final stage trains the full logxi in [-3,5] window.
initialization_proposals.rationale: Standard continuation-in-parameter: each stage is a small perturbation of a converged solution, so it tests whether the uncertainty-neutral economy (where the level non-identification is weakest and the solution should be unique) continues into a unique robust economy. If the neutral cold solve itself is degenerate, that isolates the failure to the base model rather than to robustness -- diagnostic value either way.

initialization_proposals.name: Full-green BGP analytic init with damage-shape correction (repaired analytic arm)
initialization_proposals.construction: Initialize v = logK + w(Z) - kappa(xi, lambda_3) * logN(Y) + c, where logK + w(Z) comes from the deterministic two-capital AK closed form (unit logK slope, w(Z) from the Z = 1 BGP with a quadratic interior correction), and the -logN(Y) term gives V_y the sign and curvature of the damage function per regime (regime-correct lambda_3 slope). Fit c per regime so that V' - V ~ 0 against the arm's own trained successors (combining with proposal 1's anchor). Controls from FOCs as above.
initialization_proposals.rationale: The analytic arm failed for a diagnosable reason -- level without shape -- not because analytic structure is useless. Adding the two known shape ingredients (unit capital slope, damage-function curvature) plus the jump-consistency constant costs a closed-form evaluation and directly tests the study log's own conjecture that 'a shape-aware variant would be the fix'.
